claims.text: The feedstock is cobalt-free, mechanically alloyed AlCrFeNiSi powder.
Mechanically alloyed AlCrFeNiSi tends to segregate and develop high residual stresses when processed by full-melting techniques.
Binder jetting and 3D ink extrusion can shape a binder-containing powder green body that is subsequently densified by isothermal sintering.
A solid-state sintering route can be applied to mechanically alloyed MPEA powder feedstock as an alternative to laser powder-bed fusion.
Below-melting-point isothermal sintering promotes full inter-particle diffusion without full melting.
Switching from laser-based full melting to binder jetting or ink extrusion followed by sintering reduces thermal gradients.
Avoiding rapid melt-solidification limits compositional segregation.
Isothermal sintering can produce a structurally homogeneous, uniformly inter-diffused microstructure with minimal compositional gradients.
The proposed route produces a fine-grained microstructure.
Binder jetting or ink extrusion followed by isothermal sintering lowers residual stress relative to laser-based processing.
Particles coalesce slowly during isothermal sintering.
Slow particle coalescence prevents segregation and lowers defect formation.
Sintered AlCrFeNiSi samples will contain fewer hot cracks and pores than LPBF samples.
Reduced segregation, residual stress, and defects will improve the mechanical integrity of AlCrFeNiSi.
Sintered AlCrFeNiSi samples will have higher tensile strength than conventionally fabricated LPBF samples.
Sintered AlCrFeNiSi samples will have higher ductility than conventionally fabricated LPBF samples.
Conventional LPBF AlCrFeNiSi typically exhibits compositional segregation, high residual stress, and defect-related mechanical impairment.
The effectiveness of the proposed route may vary with powder morphology, sintering profile, and build scale.
